analysis_notes.gap_analysis_detail: Torah 100 (LM2) is an extremely brief reported saying — three sentences — not a structured conceptual discourse. The text contains no explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת / הוּא / נִקְרָא used as bechina markers). The content is a practical oral teaching that true righteousness requires hitbodedut (הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת — secluded personal conversation with God), supported by citation of many famous true Tzaddikim and the example of David HaMelech. The one near-bechina statement is that Sefer Tehillim is the 'עִקָּר' (essence/core) of David's practice of hitbodedut/heart-breaking before God — but this is expressed as a descriptive identity ('זֶהוּ עִקָּר סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים שֶׁיָּסַד'), not as a formal bechina declaration. The reference to Baal Shem Tov's descendants being from 'זֶרַע דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ' is a genealogical/historical claim, not a bechina relationship. No bechina edges were recorded in the dataset for reference 1100, and the source text confirms none should have been. No missing nodes are identified.
analysis_notes.evil_mirror_check: No evil polarity exists in this Torah. The teaching is a positive practical directive — the importance of hitbodedut for genuine righteousness. No opposing evil force is named or implied.
